eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
title: Small real tanh MLP (~1-2k parameters): does it reach 55 % BER reduction?
question: Does a real-valued MLP on [Re, Im] of the window with one tanh hidden layer and about 1.8k parameters (window 15 or 17) reach 55 % BER reduction on test (external reference: 4.3e-3 at 9.71e-3 raw, about 1.8k parameters)? Also windows 21-31 with 16-32 neurons.
protocol: as E025 F10 ref_current: model real_mlp (layers 1, tanh, Xavier normal x 1, zero bias), Adam constant lr 1e-3, 200k steps, 5 seeds, selection by validation (test_reduction_valbest_select)
rm: repository convention 2 W h + 2 h (tanh, biases 0 RM), as F10 (6400 RM)
metric_note: BER reduction against raw on the window centres of each window (edge W//2), as in all runner experiments

reference.F10: E025: window 31, 1 x 100 tanh, 6502 parameters, 42.0 +- 1.6 % (5 seeds, 200k)
reference.external: colleagues: raw 9.71e-3, compact models 4.3e-3 (~1.8k parameters, ~55.7 %), 11k parameters 2.41e-3 (~75.2 %) (сообщено автором, не проверено)

rule_draft.reached: a configuration reaches 55 % if its mean test reduction (5 seeds) >= 55 %; 'close' if 55 % is within 2 std of the mean; otherwise not reached
rule_draft.limits: one recipe (no tuning: the F10 recipe), 200k steps; the external number is on other test files

value_filter.changes_next_step: yes: tells whether the external compact result is reproducible with a plain real MLP on our data
value_filter.needed_for_main_claim: reference for the MLP family at ~1-2k RM
